swagger.formSub: Test an HTTP API against its Swagger/OpenAPI spec: agnts plans the cases, sends real requests and reports a verdict per case with the evidence.
swagger.specHint: A Swagger UI, Springdoc or Redoc page works too: agnts finds the spec behind it. Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.x, up to 5 MB.
swagger.specChoose: This page offers several specs. Pick one:
swagger.baseUrlHint: Where requests go. It starts as the spec's server, which often is production: check it. A host name or an IP, on any port. Internal hosts need a Private network route.
swagger.untickedSideEffect: Left unticked: its name suggests it changes something ({word})
swagger.authHint: Use a test account's token, never a personal or production one. It is sealed, never shown again, and deleted when the ticket closes.
swagger.writeOnHint: Also POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE
swagger.writeConfirmNeeded: Confirm the base URL is not production to send write requests.
swagger.readOnlyNote: Read-only means only GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, not harmless: some APIs change things on GET. That is your call.
swagger.lockoutNote: The no-token and wrong-token cases can look like a login attack to a firewall. A test sends at most 3 of them, but it may still lock the test account or get the caller's address blocked. Behind a Private network, that address is the workspace's VPN connection, which GitLab and other tests also use.
swagger.repositoryHint: With one, agnts reads the handlers to explain failures, and failures can become a Bug or Code ticket.
swagger.notesPh: For example: user 42 is a test account; orders need an existing product id
swagger.claudeOnly: Swagger tests always run on {agent}'s light model, whatever model the workspace codes with.
swagger.noRun: No results yet: the test is running or has not run.
swagger.agntsCheckHint: agnts checked this response against the spec's schema itself
swagger.truncated: The body was cut at 64 KB
swagger.bugIntro: The Swagger test {key} of {base} found these failures:
swagger.newFailures: {n, plural, one {# new failure} other {# new failures}} since the last run
swagger.noNewFailures: No new failures since the last run
swagger.rerunTokenNeeded: New token (required: the old one was deleted when the ticket closed)
swagger.runningSub: agnts plans the cases and sends real requests to the base URL. Results appear here when the run ends.
swagger.queuedSub: Start it when you are ready.
swagger.suitesLede: Saved Swagger tests that run again on a schedule or after each deploy. Each run is a new ticket, compared with the suite's last run, and reuses its plan, so repeat runs cost fewer turns.
swagger.suitesEmpty: No suites yet. Open a finished Swagger test and save it as a suite.
swagger.saveSuiteHint: Run this test again on a schedule or after each deploy. The suite keeps its own copy of the token.
swagger.busy: The last run is still going
swagger.deleteConfirm: Delete the suite {name}? Its past runs stay.
swagger.hookHint: POST this URL from your deploy pipeline, with no body, to run the suite after each deploy. It is shown once; making a new one stops the old.
swagger.specAuth: The spec link needs a sign-in
swagger.specAuthHint: Sent with the spec fetch to the spec's host only, and not stored.
swagger.specAuthNeeded: The spec URL answered 401/403: give the token it needs, then read it again.
swagger.specAuthReused: The API requests use this token too. Change it here if they need another.
swagger.specLoginNeeded: The spec link asks for a login and password: enter them, then read it again.
swagger.specLoginHint: Opens the spec link only, and is not stored. The agent's API requests use the token under Authentication below.
swagger.nothingToShow: Nothing failed or was blocked. Show all cases to see the rest.
swagger.casesHidden: {n, plural, one {# endpoint} other {# endpoints}} without failures hidden
swagger.whatToTestPh: For example: only the POST endpoints under /v1/orders and /v1/payments; check validation errors and unknown ids. User 42 is a test account.
swagger.whatToTestHint: agnts tests only what you write here. To test exact endpoints instead, tick them below.
swagger.whatToTestNeeded: Write what to test, or tick the endpoints to test.
swagger.endpointsOptionalHint: Ticked endpoints are tested exactly as ticked. With none ticked, the text above decides what is tested.
swagger.noneTicked: none ticked: the text above decides
